headline: Russian drone hits central Kherson medical facility on first morning after Oleshky ceasefire ends, no casualties reported
dek: On the first morning after the six-day Oleshky local ceasefire expired (22:59 Kyiv Nov 1), Russian forces attacked central Kherson with drones at about 07:40 Nov 2; one drone hit a medical facility, damaging several rooms and shattering windows and interior doors, with no casualties reported…
sources: Yaroslav Shanko, deputy head of Kherson Oblast State Administration / head of Kherson City Military Administration, via Ukrinform and NV; Suspilne aftermath footage
fault_line: Was the Oleshky truce a humanitarian success or a regroup window? General Staff says Russia rotated troops and restocked; the first post-truce morning brought a drone into a Kherson medical facility.

sections.what_happened: On the first morning after the six-day Oleshky local ceasefire expired (22:59 Kyiv Nov 1), Russian forces attacked central Kherson with drones at about 07:40 Nov 2; one drone hit a medical facility, damaging several rooms and shattering windows and interior doors, with no casualties reported preliminarily. Public broadcaster Suspilne showed the aftermath. Shanko also reported FPV, Mavic reconnaissance and Molniya attack drones operating in the Kherson community, and said Russian artillery and drone attacks had struck Kherson and Antonivka over the previous day, damaging residential buildings and injuring 2 people. Ukraine's General Staff said Russian forces used the humanitarian pause to strengthen positions (already recorded at 1400-03). Wider overnight context (Ukrainian Air Force, as of 08:00 Nov 2): 193 drones launched from 18:00 Nov 1, 154 neutralised, strikes recorded at 26 locations, debris at 9.
sections.what_verified: Ukrinform (T2, STATE UA) carries Shanko's statement; NV (T3) independently reports the same Shanko statement and the Suspilne aftermath footage. Two distinct publisher families, both tracing to the same Ukrainian official -- attribution to Shanko is mandatory, not independent confirmation of the strike itself.
sections.what_disputed: No Russian statement on the medical-facility hit in-window; the strike itself is attested only via the Ukrainian official + Suspilne footage, not by an independent monitor. Distinguish from 1800-03 (Korabelny car drone hit, 2 injured, ~08:00 Monday) -- a separate incident the same morning, not the same strike.
sections.why_matters: The longest pause of the war ended at 22:59 Sunday; by 07:40 Monday a drone hit a Kherson medical facility -- the truce's first morning, measured in hours, not days.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (NV 15:00+02 = 17:00 ; United24/Ukrinform same-day; absent from all Nov 2 scans before 1900) -- Post-truce Kherson: Russian drone hits central Kherson medical facility on first morning after Oleshky ceasefire ends, no casualties reported

totw_analysis: Our read: The longest pause of the war ended at 22:59 Sunday; by 07:40 Monday a drone hit a Kherson medical facility -- the truce's first morning, measured in hours, not days. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Was the Oleshky truce a humanitarian success or a regroup window? General Staff says Russia rotated troops and restocked; the first post-truce morning brought a drone into a Kherson medical facility.
